newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight business routine, more orders awaite.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight business routine, more orders awaite.

text.p: Business was routine on the sugar freight market on Tuesday after the recent wave of activity but more orders should emerge soon due to a number of physical buying tenders, shipbrokers said.
Of the day's firmer business, Fiji Sugar Marketing was reported to have fixed its earlier 1/10 April order for 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Fiji to London at a rate in the low $30 bracket.
Cargill fixed 16,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Rio Haina to US Gulf/Atlantic for 20 March onwards but no rate has yet been reported.
New business included E D & F Man, which quoted for 23,300 tonnes of bulk sugar from Corinto to Casablanca plus options for 25/31 March.
Shipbrokers said Sucre Export's 12/13,000-tonne bagged cargo destined for Algeria was loading at Dunkirk not Calais, as originally specified.
In other news, Iran bought 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar for shipment in May from a France-based trade house.
Bangladesh bought 25,000 tonnes of white sugar for shipment by May 1, with the first instalment of 12,500 tonnes expected to reach Chittagong by April 25.
It also called for offers to supply a total of 50,000 tonnes of sugar for shipment by June 9 in two tenders scheduled for March 22 and 29.
Traders said the tender's terms specifed that the sugar should be delivered in four equal shipments by May 8, 15, 29 and June 9.
Market sources said Libya was in the market to buy at least one cargo of white sugar, most likely for May shipment.
